evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: The brain of type A NPD patients is usually atrophic. Ganglion cells are often swollen, and the cytoplasm is pale and vacuolated. Within these cells are membrane-bound inclusions. There is a loss of cells in the cerebral and cerebellar cortices of type A infants, along with gliosis in both gray and white matter. Some areas of the white matter show demyelination.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.

nodes.description: Intravenous recombinant human acid sphingomyelinase (olipudase alfa; evaluated across pediatric NCT02292654 and adult NCT02004691 step-up debulking dose-escalation trials to avoid acute ceramide-release toxicity) is approved for non-central nervous system manifestations of ASMD across subtypes, reducing sphingomyelin storage in liver, spleen, and lung. However, intravenous olipudase alfa does not cross the blood-brain barrier and therefore does not prevent or slow the relentless central nervous system neurodegeneration of NPD-A.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: In these models the common type NPD A mutation – R496L, and the common type B mutation – deltaR608 were introduced. The phenotypes of these mice were as expected. R496L mice developed a severe "type A" phenotype indistinguishable from the knockout mice. DeltaR608 developed a later onset, non-neurological "type B" phenotype. They expressed between ~5 and 10% residual ASM activity in the brain, again demonstrating that low level ASM activity was neuroprotective.

nodes.description: Biallelic severe loss-of-function variants in SMPD1 (sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 1) abolish or reduce lysosomal acid sphingomyelinase activity to well below 10% of normal controls (and below the ~5–10% residual central nervous system activity threshold seen in non-neuronopathic type B alleles). Acid sphingomyelinase normally hydrolyzes sphingomyelin into ceramide and phosphocholine within lysosomes and at stressed plasma-membrane microdomains; its profound loss is the initiating molecular defect of NPD-A.
